summary: The Decreasing Russian Oil Profits Act of 2025 requires the President to impose economic sanctions on foreign persons who buy, import, facilitate transactions for, support, or manage entities dealing in crude oil or petroleum products originating from the Russian Federation. The bill provides specific potential exceptions related to countries that restrict Russian funds, deposit funds into accounts to benefit Ukraine, support Ukraine economically or militarily, or use temporary port-specific exceptions under certain conditions. The bill includes rules regarding price caps and sets a five-year sunset on the provisions.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to property-blocking sanctions that prohibit transactions involving property and interests in property within the United States or under the control of a U.S. person.
affected_groups.group: Foreign persons dealing in Russian crude oil or petroleum products

affected_groups.effect: Subject to the same property-blocking sanctions as entities directly engaging in prohibited Russian oil trade.
affected_groups.group: Chief executive officers and board members of entities trading in Russian oil

affected_groups.effect: May qualify for exceptions from sanctions if they meet specific criteria, such as restricting payments for Russian oil to accounts used strictly for food and medicine, depositing funds into accounts to support Ukraine, or providing significant economic or military support to Ukraine.
affected_groups.group: Governments and entities of countries purchasing Russian oil

key_provisions: Requires the President to impose property-blocking sanctions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act on foreign persons determined to be involved in purchasing, importing, or facilitating trade in Russian crude oil or petroleum products.
Applies sanctions to chief executive officers and board members of entities involved in prohibited Russian oil trade activities.

Allows the President to apply up to two specific exception frameworks, such as exceptions for countries that isolate Russian funds for limited humanitarian use and reduce purchases, or countries that make deposits into an account for the benefit of Ukraine.

Excludes price-cap-violating maritime transport and related services (like shipping, insuring, and financing) from benefiting from the permitted exception frameworks, regardless of whether the service provider is based in a Group of 7 country.
Establishes a 5-year sunset date on all provisions and sanctions imposed under this Act.

The bill provides specific potential exceptions related to countries that restrict Russian funds, deposit funds into accounts to benefit Ukraine, support Ukraine economically or militarily, or use temporary port-specific exceptions under certain conditions. The bill includes rules regarding price caps and sets a five-year sunset on the provisions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes mandatory sanctions targeting global trade in Russian crude oil and petroleum products, with structured exceptions tied to foreign policy actions regarding Ukraine. The significance score reflects substantial potential changes for international entities trading in Russian energy products, depending on presidential implementation of exceptions and enforcement.
